comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> If I want to create MSI using another tool - what folder contents I need to use? just .exe file?

Yes. Unless you use the sidecar or resource features, then you gotta bundle them manually too.

> don't know why it is trying to load tauri.localhost?

This is the dummy localhost address tauri serves the frontend files from (it's not an actual localhost _server_).

> after changing ""distDir": "../dist" - instead of blank - I am seeing below

Sounds like your ../dist dir was empty or didn't contain an `index.html` file

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> We have advanced installer license , which we can integrate in build pipelines as well. Build output of tauri is just single .exe file only? I need clarity on what are the files we need to include!!

I can't go into more detail than above since i don't know your project. If you use the [sidecar](https://tauri.app/v1/guides/building/sidecar/) or [resource](https://tauri.app/v1/guides/building/resources) features then you'll have to bundle these files yourself. If you don't use them then you only need the .exe from `target/release/`...

----

`"../dist/..web"` this one sounds correct, it's what we set in create-tauri-app too: https://github.com/tauri-apps/create-tauri-app/blob/dev/packages/cli/fragments/fragment-angular/_cta_manifest_#L8

Can you try a debug build via `npm run tauri build -- --debug` (or `yarn build --debug`) and run the .exe from (`target/debug/`) and check the devtools console (right click on the window -> inspect) for errors please?
Note that `tauri dev` and `tauri build --debug` is _not_ the same.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The relevant people are/were on vacation and have a lot of catching up to do, apologies for the delay.

That said, i didn't see your message before that so i can answer this myself:
> we are using self signed certificate attached - which is not recognized by tauri/webview used. how do we fix this issue

Tauri currently does indeed not support self signed certificates at all right now. Here's a discussion on workarounds: https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/4039 (tldr: Use Rust for the requests)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1  - Thanks for reply.
Two solutions discussed in this thread mainly.
1. Catching the error and ignoring,  app.on('certificate-error') - do we have this event on tauri framework?
2. Modifying the framework code to ignore this error - Is this change merged to master - I can use latest version?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
1. No we don't, reason: https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/4039#issuecomment-1115930694 and https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/4039#issuecomment-1116130793
2. Also no. Note that if we'd add that to Tauri, it would only apply to the http client in `@tauri-apps/api`, not the browser's default fetch. The Rust solutions discussed there were meant as a solution on the user's side (via [tauri commands](https://tauri.app/v1/guides/features/command)), not inside tauri.
